data.why: The calculator is a stateless form with no sample-data files in the repo; a 'Load inputs...' JSON upload exists on the page, so a values file built from tests/fixtures/scipy_reference_values.json (and test_chemical.py's worked example) lets the browser agent load a known-good scenario in one click instead of typing every field.

goals: Enter reactor geometry and flow conditions and compute the reactor's Reynolds number, Peclet number, and the laminar/transitional/turbulent and advection/diffusion regime verdicts needed to validate the RTD model's assumptions
Enter a microbial rate constant k and average fluence rate Eavg and compute the predicted C/C0 (log inactivation) for the segregated-flow (RTD) model versus the well-mixed approximation
Given a measured C/C0 from a validation run, back-solve for the rate constant k (single point or a batch of C/C0, Eavg pairs) consistent with that observation
Sweep Eavg over a range and inspect the resulting dose-response curve (RTD vs well-mixed) and its fitted exponential slope on a chart

Switch to chemical actinometry mode, derive kp from wavelength, absorption cross-section and quantum yield, and feed it into the same RTD engine to back-solve average fluence rate from a measured conversion
Save a given set of inputs to a JSON file and reload them later to reproduce a calculation exactly

review.summary: The tree is accurate and well structured: it captures this laminar-flow UV-reactor validation tool's real stages (regime check, RTD vs well-mixed prediction, back-solving k or E', actinometry, reproducibility), and nine of the eleven screens I opened match their nodes. It needs fixes before filing: two citations show nothing of what they claim, f1 and f2 overstate the tooltip and banner behaviour, f4 is generic Plotly, and the shared metadata tooltip/glossary feature and the chemical forward-prediction task are missing.
